stories.title: Wally the Wi‑Fi Router Shares the Signal
stories.teaser: In the corner of the living room, a little box blinks quietly. It is sending invisible waves all around your home. Who is Wally, and how does he help your tablet reach the whole world?
learning_objectives: Wi‑Fi helps devices connect to the internet without wires
A router sends and receives Wi‑Fi signals
Signals carry data (information)
Distance and walls can make Wi‑Fi weaker
Passwords help keep Wi‑Fi private

pages.text: In the living room, a tiny box blinks—Wally the Wi‑Fi router. He’s ready to share internet signals around the home.
pages.image_prompt: Friendly Wi‑Fi router with blinking lights on a small table, cozy room Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Wally sends invisible waves through the air. These waves are Wi‑Fi signals that nearby devices can listen to.
pages.image_prompt: Curved Wi‑Fi waves spreading from router toward phone, tablet, laptop Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Phones and tablets connect to Wally. Then they can send data, like messages, pictures, and questions, to the internet.
pages.image_prompt: Devices linking to router with dotted lines, data icons floating Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: A router is like a helper bridge. It passes data between your home devices and the bigger internet outside.
pages.image_prompt: Simple bridge metaphor: router as bridge between home and cloud internet Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Walls and long distance can make signals weaker. Closer devices often get faster, stronger Wi‑Fi.
pages.image_prompt: Split scene: strong signal nearby, weaker signal behind wall Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Sometimes too many devices share at once. Wally works hard, but waiting turns can help everyone connect smoothly.
pages.image_prompt: Many devices with gentle 'turn-taking' icons, friendly network scene Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: A Wi‑Fi password is like a secret key. It helps keep strangers from joining your home network.
pages.image_prompt: Key and lock icons next to Wi‑Fi symbol, safe and friendly Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: Grown-ups choose the password and settings. People stay in charge of what connects and when.
pages.image_prompt: Adult adjusting router settings on a phone, shield icon Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: When the router restarts, the signal may pause. Then Wally wakes up and sends waves again.
pages.image_prompt: Router turning off/on with a small restart arrow, calm tone Flat pastel illustration, kid-friendly, simple shapes, soft shading, 1:1 aspect ratio.

pages.text: At bedtime, Wally’s lights glow softly. Quiet signals keep ready, so devices can connect again tomorrow.
